title: Opening one panel at 1024-1279 px hides the other panel for good, also on wide screens
detail: From 1024 to 1279 px only one side panel docks (oneDock). setPanels forces the other panel closed, and because neither panel is a drawer at these widths it writes that forced state into dockPref, which is saved. Example: at 1200 px, open the tools panel. The Inspector closes, and hideRight: true is saved. Widen the window to 1440 px, or reload there: the Inspector stays hidden. It works the other way too: pressing ] at 1200 px saves hideLeft: true. In v14 the right panel was a drawer below 1280 px, so this never touched the saved choice. This is a regression for laptop users who also use a large monitor.
evidence: work/xva/test/rvreg_cdp/cmd/states.js (result: panel sequence 1440 start {savedR:false} -> 1200 tools opened {hideR:true, savedR:true} -> 1440 after {hideR:true} -> 1440 reload {hideR:true}); src/app.js setPanels (around line 11811) and oneDock
fix: When oneDock() forces a panel closed, treat it as run-time only: update dockPref only for the panel the user toggled, not for the panel the rule closed. Then re-apply dockPref when the width reaches 1280 px or more, in the resize handler that already handles drawers.

title: v15_planemenu_cmd.js fails after the phone merge: its touch-pan check presses under the Y inset
detail: Check 7 ('touch: a pan first (40 px) pans and opens nothing') presses at the bottom-left corner of X on a 390 px phone (L.l + 24, L.t + L.h - 24). After the phone layout merged, the Y inset (ph-swap, 116 x 116) covers that point. The gesture lands on the inset, so the view does not pan (v0 == v1 == {cx:0, cy:0, s:60}). Panning works elsewhere. The test was not re-run after the phone merge, so the merged build ships with a failing acceptance file. The phone report says its own test passes, which is true, but this one fails.
fix: Move the touch-pan check to a free part of X (for example the middle of the upper half), or read the inset rectangle and avoid it. Re-run every v15_*_cmd.js file after each merge.

title: zp_cmd.js was pinned to the v14 geometry to pass; at the shipped geometry one check fails on ruler pixels
detail: zp_cmd.js now sets window.__cmwChainH = 272 ('its per-pixel truth counts the axes as pixels'). With the hook off (the real 188 px chain), it fails one check: 'exact at rest after the drag' finds 66 bad pixels out of 6110, all in row 584 at x = 8..38, colour [46,61,71]. That is the bottom ruler band of the taller pane, not a wrong image. So the image is fine, but the zero-and-pole acceptance no longer covers the layout users get. This test was changed to fit, not fixed.
evidence: <tmp> (copy with __cmwChainH = 0); diff of test/zp_cmd.js against the main tree
fix: Mask the ruler bands (or the pane border rows) in the per-pixel truth and drop the geometry hook from zp_cmd.js. Keep the hook only in the quality and perf suites, where the goldens and baselines require it.

title: tour_cmd.js: the Phase callout now covers the panel (93 of 94)
detail: The check 'Phase portrait: the callout is below the panel, not over it' fails. The callout card is at t 54..296, over the panes at t 44..696. The tour build reported this check as already failing. It is likely tied to the taller v15 planes (a 188 px chain leaves less room under the panel). I did not check it against v14 within the time box. All other tour checks pass, and so does i18n_cmd (95 of 95).
fix: Run tour_cmd.js against v15-base to confirm whether this fails there too. If it is new, let the callout fall back to the side of the panel when there is no room below it.

title: Landscape centre readout shows 7.11×10⁻¹⁵ i instead of 0 at the new geometry
detail: ubfix_cmd 'landscape: the centre ray meets the helicoid axis' (example 13, the pointer at the centre of X) passed at the v14 gate. It now reads 'z 0.0000 + 7.11×10⁻¹⁵i': with the taller pane, the centre ray lands a rounding error off the axis. The readout then shows a fixed 0.0000 next to a scientific-notation 10⁻¹⁵. The 21 other ubfix failures were already failing at the v14 gate (stale checks of older UI), and its 'no console errors' failure is 404s for the kit's gl-helpers.html, which work/xva/dist does not have.
evidence: <tmp> notes/gate-v14-r1/evidence/ubfix_cmd.json (same 21 older failures, without this one)
fix: In the readout, print a component as 0 when it is below about 1e-12 of |z| (or of the view's scale). Refresh or retire ubfix_cmd.js, so that a real regression in it is not lost among 21 stale failures.

title: About 190 lines of dead code and dead CSS from the old cards and the Guarantees panel
detail: These are no longer called: buildProps (app.js 9174-9264), fillProps (10114-10172), renderRail (9051), openCardPop (8250-8277), with PROPS.el, PROPS.texF and PROPS.rail. refreshZpCard still queries '.card-pop' and '#pipeline .card .params', which no longer exist. page.html still styles .pchip, .pchips, .ftex-row, .btag, .card-pop, .rail-lamps and .rl. params.js has an unused 'renderT' (let renderT = 0 ... void renderT). They were probably kept on purpose so that the 3-way merge with v14's fixes stays clean.
evidence: work/xva/src/app.js (grep: each function is defined but never called); work/xva/src/page.html; work/xva/src/params.js:418,426
fix: Delete them right after the v14 merge, in one commit with no other changes.

title: Latent leak: a rebuilt Inspector would mount Parameters again and keep drawing the old copy
detail: inspector.js skeleton() rebuilds the panel whenever #propsPanel no longer holds its section. It then sets mounted = false and calls Params.mount again. The old mount is never destroyed. Params.render skips a mount only when '!m.el.isConnected && m.el.parentNode == null'. A detached old mount still has a parent (the old wrapper), so every change redraws it. Today only the dead buildProps clears #propsPanel, so this cannot happen yet. It will as soon as anything else clears the host (a language switch without reload, or a phone re-park).
fix: Keep the handle Params.mount returns and call destroy() before mounting again. In Params.render, skip any mount whose element is not connected.

title: t_sound.js fails (63 or 64 of 66): a v14 bug that the main tree has fixed
detail: 'queue: the clock moves 1 (2) render quanta mid-burst' gives 9 bells instead of 8. src/sound.js is unchanged from v15-base. The main tree's sound.js fixes it (q.due queue), and t_sound passes 66/66 there. It comes in with the planned 3-way merge. It is not a v15 regression.
fix: None in xva; confirm t_sound passes after the merge.

title: The perf and quality suites never see the shipped plane size; measured by hand it is within budget
detail: Both suites pin the v14 geometry through __cmwChainH = 272, as required, so the goldens and baselines stay valid. So they cannot catch a cost from the taller v15 planes (a 188 px chain adds about 13% more plane pixels at 1440 x 900). I measured at the real geometry: 1440 x 900, dpr 1, 4 steps (zp, Möbius, z², exp), 5 cards visible, load average 4-20. Slider of a (used by a zero and a radius), work per frame p95: X → Y 3.9-4.3 ms, Phase 1.6-1.9, Landscape 1.6-2.7, Deformation 2.7-6.0. rAF p95 16.8 ms (60 fps), and no long tasks in 11 of 12 runs (one 65 ms task in the Deformation). Zero drag: p95 4.1-4.2 ms in v15 against 3.5-3.8 ms in v14. Shape drag in X → Y: p95 11.9-13.7 ms in v15 against 11.8-12.2 ms in v14, close to the 14 ms budget in both. The max frame in one v15 run was 24 ms (rAF max 117 ms), and one v14 run also showed 33 ms intervals. This is noise-level, with no clear regression. The cards' redraw after release added no dropped frames (rAF max 16.8 ms).
fix: Optional: add one perf unit that runs at the shipped geometry (no hook), with its own new baseline, so the real layout is watched from v15 on. Never change the existing baselines.

title: English: a few new strings are unidiomatic or inconsistent
detail: Guide, 'The planes' menu': 'Then come what is under the pointer (a zero or pole, a shape, a cut handle), Add zero ... here' has a broken verb and list. Guide, Guarantees: 'one not named is only not implied, not false'. The tour says the same: 'one not listed is only not implied'. Both read awkwardly. Tour, 'Add a zero here': 'Behind other steps the zero is placed where the point lands' (it means after the earlier steps). Parameters: '= {v}, by formula of {x}' and the menu item 'Make free' are terse. The rail button says 'Edit the selected step', but the selection can be F or the region. Messages for the same action disagree: the Inspector announces 'Added a zero of f₂', the plane menu 'Added zero of f₂ at 1+i', and Remove says 'Removed zero ζ₁ of f₁.' with a full stop.
evidence: work/xva/src/app.js:11660 (guide), 11676 (Guarantees), 2687; work/xva/src/tour.js (Add a zero here, Guarantees); work/xva/src/params.js:506, 573; work/xva/src/planemenu.js:233, 282; work/xva/src/page.html (rightRailEdit)
fix: Suggested: 'Below that come the items for what is under the pointer (a zero or pole, a shape, a cut handle), then Add zero ...'; 'a property not named is not implied, though it may still hold'; 'After earlier steps, the zero goes where the point lands, so it stays exact'; '= {v}, from {x}'; 'Unlink from the formula'; 'Edit the selection'; use one pattern, 'Added zero ζ₃ of f₂ at 1+i.' / 'Removed zero ζ₁ of f₁.'. Update the Russian table to match.
